summary: Jean-Luc Boissoneault, a former world-level bodybuilder and founder of Free Form Fitness who trained some of Canada's wealthiest entrepreneurs, explains to David DiNardo why his purpose is helping men reclaim personal sovereignty. He traces how chasing optimal health for clients led him from exercise to nutrition to stress and finally to meditation, which he practiced up to three hours a day in a backyard yurt before selling his business and moving to an island. The conversation covers what separated a billionaire client from grinders who suffered heart attacks, how fear drives entrepreneurs to avoid decisions, and why solitude and blunt mentors are the fastest routes to self-knowledge.
takeaways: You cannot change your thoughts with more thoughts; Jean-Luc committed to 90 straight days of meditation because entrepreneurs have to stop thinking their way out of problems and create space to see their own patterns.
Meditation is just sitting with what is for five minutes a day with no desired outcome; consistency matters far more than technique, and it works like the gym.

He caps his clients at 180 working days a year because forced time off exposes work addiction, pressure-tests whether the business runs without the founder, and produces the higher perspective needed to fire the wrong person or drop the wrong work.

The traits that set billionaire Mattamy Homes founder Peter Gilgan apart were planning ahead with a reverse-engineered org chart, putting health and workouts before business, knowing his genius and delegating everything else, and leading by inspiration rather than dictation.

Most fear traces back to a single trunk, fear of death, branching into fear of judgment, rejection and being cast out; the coaching move is to ask what could change today and then do it, such as picking up the phone and making sales calls on the spot.

Jean-Luc scores clients on five freedoms: health, time, money, purpose and relationships, and rejects six-figure job offers because his life is already designed around his own gift, one-on-one coaching.

The two fastest routes to self-knowledge are solitude in nature with no phone and the company of a strong, honest man who will tell you when you are off your path, as his first mentor did by forcing him to set a deadline to open his gym.
